authority: Ministry of Women and Child Development

description.en: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) is a maternity benefit programme under which a cash incentive of Rs. 5,000 is provided in three installments directly to the bank or post office account of pregnant women and lactating mothers for the first living child. The scheme aims to provide partial compensation for wage loss during pregnancy and childbirth, promote safe delivery and good nutrition practices, and improve the health of the mother and child. The benefit is provided through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account. The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development through the Anganwadi services infrastructure at the state and district level.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All women applying for PMMVY maternity benefit
verifiedConditions.claim: The maternity benefit of Rs. 5,000 under PMMVY is available for the first living child of the pregnant woman or lactating mother. Women who already have a living child are not eligible for this benefit under the original PMMVY guidelines.

The applicant must be a pregnant woman or a lactating mother. The first installment is claimed after registration of pregnancy at the Anganwadi Centre (AWC) or approved health facility. Registration must occur within 150 days of the last menstrual period (LMP).

unverifiedEligibility: Under PMMVY 2.0, the scheme has been expanded to provide Rs. 5,000 for the second child if the second child is a girl, subject to revised guidelines.
Women employed in the Central Government or State Government or PSU who receive paid maternity leave may be excluded.
Women who are beneficiaries under similar state-level maternity benefit schemes may or may not be eligible simultaneously depending on state integration.

requirements.claim: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card issued by the Anganwadi Centre or approved health facility, showing registration of pregnancy and antenatal check-up details. The MCP card serves as the primary record for tracking the beneficiary's eligibility for each installment.

Aadhaar card of the beneficiary (pregnant woman / lactating mother). Aadhaar is mandatory for identification and for DBT payment. If Aadhaar is not available, alternative identity proof such as voter ID or bank passbook may be accepted temporarily pending Aadhaar enrollment.

Bank account or post office savings account in the name of the beneficiary, linked to Aadhaar for Direct Benefit Transfer. The account number and IFSC code must be provided. Joint accounts with the husband are also accepted in some states.

Pregnancy registration certificate from the Anganwadi Centre (AWC) or approved health facility. Registration should be done within 150 days of the last menstrual period (LMP). This is required for the first installment of Rs. 1,000.

Record of at least one antenatal check-up (ANC) after six months of pregnancy. The ANC record on the MCP card must be verified by the Anganwadi worker or health facility. This is required for the second installment of Rs. 2,000.

Child birth registration certificate and record of the child receiving the first cycle of vaccinations (BCG, OPV, DPT, and Hepatitis B or their equivalent). This is required for the third installment of Rs. 2,000.

processInformation.claim: Register pregnancy at the nearest Anganwadi Centre (AWC) or approved health facility within 150 days of the last menstrual period. The Anganwadi worker or ASHA (Accredited Social Health Activist) helps fill the PMMVY application form (Form 1-A) and enters the details on the PMMVY-CAS (Common Application Software) portal or mobile app.

Claim installments at the designated milestones: First installment (Rs. 1,000) after pregnancy registration; Second installment (Rs. 2,000) after at least one antenatal check-up at six months of pregnancy; Third installment (Rs. 2,000) after child birth registration and first cycle of vaccinations. Each claim requires submission of the respective form (Form 1-A, 1-B, or 1-C) with supporting documents.

The Anganwadi worker verifies the documents and enters data in the PMMVY-CAS system. The claim is approved by the CDPO (Child Development Project Officer) or designated approving authority at the block or district level. On approval, the payment is processed through PFMS (Public Financial Management System) for DBT to the beneficiary's account.

The approved installment amount is transferred directly to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account or post office account via PFMS. The beneficiary receives an SMS notification on the registered mobile number confirming the credit. Payment status can be tracked on the PMMVY portal or through the Anganwadi worker.

output.claim: A total maternity benefit of Rs. 5,000 paid in three installments via Direct Benefit Transfer to the beneficiary's bank or post office account. First installment of Rs. 1,000 on registration of pregnancy, second installment of Rs. 2,000 after antenatal check-up at six months, and third installment of Rs. 2,000 after child birth registration and first-cycle vaccinations. The remaining Rs. 1,000 (to make the total Rs. 6,000 as per the National Food Security Act) is provided under the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) for institutional delivery.

fees.claim: There is no application fee for PMMVY. The scheme is entirely funded by the Central Government (shared with State Governments in the ratio of 60:40 for states and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan states). No charges are to be collected from beneficiaries at any stage.

processingTime.applicability: From claim submission to DBT credit for each installment
processingTime.claim: Each installment claim typically takes 15-45 days from submission to credit in the beneficiary's account, depending on verification speed at the block/district level and PFMS payment processing cycles. The total duration from first registration to receipt of all three installments spans the pregnancy and early postnatal period (approximately 9-12 months).

sources.title: PMMVY — Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana Portal
sources.publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The PMMVY portal provides scheme guidelines, beneficiary registration, claim processing, and payment tracking. The scheme provides Rs. 5,000 in three installments for the first living child. Aadhaar-based DBT is the disbursement mechanism. Claims are processed through the PMMVY-CAS application software.
claimsSupported: Rs. 5,000 maternity benefit in three installments for first living child.
First installment Rs. 1,000 after pregnancy registration.
Second installment Rs. 2,000 after antenatal check-up at 6 months.
Third installment Rs. 2,000 after birth registration and first vaccinations.
sources.uncertainty: PMMVY 2.0 guidelines may expand eligibility to second child if girl child; implementation status varies by state.

sources.title: Ministry of Women and Child Development — PMMVY Scheme Details
sources.publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Ministry of Women and Child Development provides detailed scheme guidelines, implementation framework, and monitoring data for PMMVY. The scheme fulfills the provisions of the National Food Security Act 2013 which mandates maternity benefit of not less than Rs. 6,000 for every pregnant and lactating woman.
claimsSupported: PMMVY implements the maternity benefit provision of the National Food Security Act 2013.
Central-State funding ratio is 60:40 for general states and 90:10 for NE and Himalayan states.
Pregnancy registration and antenatal check-ups are mandatory milestones for installments.
Child birth registration and vaccination are required for the third installment.
sources.uncertainty: The NFSA mandates Rs. 6,000; the balance Rs. 1,000 is provided under JSY, and integration between the two schemes may vary.

limitations: The scheme benefit of Rs. 5,000 under PMMVY plus Rs. 1,000 under JSY totals Rs. 6,000 as mandated by NFSA; however, JSY benefit availability depends on institutional delivery.
PMMVY 2.0 expansion to second child (if girl) is subject to revised guidelines and state-level implementation which may not be uniform.
State-level implementation quality varies and some states may have additional maternity benefit schemes that interact with PMMVY.
The record does not detail the grievance redressal mechanism for delayed or denied payments.
Processing times are indicative and may be longer in areas with limited Anganwadi infrastructure or connectivity issues with the PMMVY-CAS system.
Women employed in the formal sector with paid maternity leave benefits are generally excluded, but verification of this exclusion varies.
